gamePage.title: The Game
gamePage.intro: First explore the documented history of Oftersheim, then discover the legend behind a fictional treasure hunt.
gamePage.historyRoman: Archaeological discoveries in the 1960s uncovered remains of at least two houses from the Roman period.
gamePage.historyFrankish: Centuries later, Frankish settlers lived in the area. One may have been Oftari, whose name is often linked to Oftersheim. He is thought to have lived here around the 7th or 8th century, though the connection is not certain.
gamePage.historyRecord: The name Oftersheim first appears in the Lorsch Codex in 766 CE. The town is about 1,250 years old, with a history reaching back well over a millennium.
gamePage.historyLinkIntro: Learn more about the town's history on
gamePage.legendDisclaimer: The story below is a modern legend inspired by local history, not a record of verified historical events.
gamePage.legendDiscovery: According to the legend, Oftari—a village leader who could read and write a little, a rare skill in his day—found a map among the fallen stones of a Roman villa. It seemed to point toward a treasure left behind in Roman times. Oftari searched in vain; at last he returned the map to its hiding place and recorded the mystery in his diary, hoping someone in the future might have better luck.
gamePage.legendOrder: Many centuries later, in the 1790s, local historians uncovered the diary during an excavation. Its pages told of the map and where it had been found. The mayor feared that word of the treasure would bring a rush of seekers and endanger the village. With a few trusted council members, he founded the Order of Keepers and removed the page that revealed the map's resting place. From then on, the secret passed quietly from one Keeper to the next.
gamePage.legendWartimeLead: For generations, the Order kept watch over Oftari's secret. Then, in the 1940s, the Nazis learned of the hidden society and began their search for the page.
gamePage.photoAlt: Black-and-white still life of a typewriter, papers, an old telephone, and photographs.
gamePage.photoCaption: An atmospheric illustration for the wartime part of the legend; this is not a documentary photograph of the events.
gamePage.legendWartimeDetail: A Nazi record preserves the words of a captured Keeper: “The diary page is where they buried their dead in ancient times.” The other Keepers acted quickly. By the time the searchers reached the place, the page was gone; all they found was a typewritten letter mocking their efforts. The page had been carried elsewhere, and its trail faded into silence.
gamePage.playDescription: The legend becomes a game: follow clues through Oftersheim and search for the hidden gem the Romans left behind, undiscovered for centuries.
gamePage.playStartingPoint: The hunt begins with the words preserved in the Nazi records: “The diary page is where they buried their dead in ancient times.” After the war, historians found the records and searched for the box the Nazis had left at the place they found it, hoping the Order might return for it. They believed “the old graveyard” meant Oftersheim's local cemetery. But the box was not there. If the clue speaks true, the old graveyard must be somewhere else—and the search continues.
gamePage.ruleOne: Do not remove, alter, or destroy any clues.
gamePage.ruleTwo: Return each hint to its place so other players can find it.
gamePage.ruleThree: Explore responsibly and respect residents, private property, and public spaces.
gamePage.ruleFour: Bring a UV light; some messages may use special ink.
